question: Why did sulphonamide resistance in British E. coli fail to fall when prescriptions dropped by 97%?
answer: Because the resistance gene was not travelling alone. UK prescribing fell through the 1990s, yet resistant E. coli from London patients rose from about 40% in 1991 to 46% in 1999. The gene sits on plasmids, mobile loops of DNA, beside genes for drugs still in use, which kept selecting the whole package.
move: Stopping one cause changes little if the result is bundled with another.
ask: What cause did I remove that changed nothing because the result came bundled with another?
reference: Enne, Livermore, Stephens & Hall, Persistence of sulphonamide resistance in Escherichia coli in the UK despite national prescribing restriction, The Lancet, 2001
